headline: Golan urges the opposition to govern with Arab parties

sources: Donald Trump (Air Force One remarks, via AFP); Benjamin Netanyahu (Likud HQ speech); Yousef Jabareen, Joint List chair (via Haaretz liveblog); Yair Golan, Democrats leader (via X, as carried by Palestine Chronicle/Dawn)
fault_line: Should Arab parties -- now at a historic 19 seats -- be allowed to make or break an Israeli government, or is a government that relies on them illegitimate?

sections.what_happened: With the CEC count at 76.8% (totw-20261028-1400-01: Netanyahu bloc 54, Eisenkot bloc 47, Arab parties 19; 61 needed), the fight has moved from ballots to coalition-building. (1) Trump, aboard Air Force One: 'I think when the endorsement went out, it had helped him a lot' (AFP via NDTV/Channels; Times/Fox carry the same quote). The QUOTE is confirmed; that the endorsement CAUSED the result is Trump's claim, not proof. (2) Netanyahu: it is 'a shame' / unthinkable to set up a government relying on 'anti-Zionist Arab parties' that 'regard Hamas as a charitable organisation' and 'call our soldiers war criminals' (Times liveblog). He had already ruled an Arab-backed government 'out of the question' in his election-night speech (Times Now). (3) Joint List chief Yousef Jabareen: his party is ready to help oust Netanyahu and calls for 'genuine Jewish-Arab partnership' as the alternative to a 'government of bloodshed' (Haaretz liveblog via Nairobi News). (4) Democrats leader Yair Golan urged his Change-camp partners to 'stop being afraid' and form a government with Arab parties participating (Palestine Chronicle/Dawn). Counterpoint, on record: Eisenkot has said he will form a 'Zionist government' and Lieberman has said 'No coalition will be formed with the Arab parties' (Tapestry summary of their positions) -- so the Arab-partner route is contested inside the opposition itself, not just by Netanyahu. Label: PRIMARY-SOURCE CLAIMS (the quotes) + ATTRIBUTED REPORT (the coalition arithmetic).
sections.what_verified: Trump quote: AFP (T1) via NDTV (AFP-attributed) + Times + Fox carries of the identical quote. Jabareen offer: Haaretz (T3) liveblog. Coalition arithmetic: Times of Israel (T3) CEC figures, already in 1400-01. Golan urge: carried by Palestine Chronicle/Dawn (no declared tier) -- reported as a carried quote, not as corroboration.
sections.what_disputed: Eisenkot's own 'Zionist government' line and Lieberman's 'no coalition with Arab parties' line block the Jabareen/Golan route from inside the opposition. No CEC final result exists yet; the 76.8% partial is not a result, and double-envelope (soldier) votes are still to be counted.
sections.why_matters: 54 seats, 7 short of power -- and now the kingmaker fight: Netanyahu calls an Arab-backed government a danger, the Joint List offers to topple him, and Trump claims his endorsement turned the tide.
sections.context: Background: MISSED CATCH-UP + IN-WINDOW COALITION FIGHT -- Israel election deadlock: Trump claims his endorsement helped Netanyahu 'a lot'; Netanyahu calls an Arab-backed government a danger; Joint List offers to help oust Netanyahu; Golan urges the opposition to govern with Arab parties

totw_analysis: Our read: 54 seats, 7 short of power -- and now the kingmaker fight: Netanyahu calls an Arab-backed government a danger, the Joint List offers to topple him, and Trump claims his endorsement turned the tide. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Should Arab parties -- now at a historic 19 seats -- be allowed to make or break an Israeli government, or is a government that relies on them illegitimate?
